title: Activity feed that pages with OFFSET through millions of rows
prompt: Activity feed with infinite scroll. Partner accounts have up to 40M events and their staff scroll deep: @Skip of
200,000 and more is common, and such a page takes 4 to 9 s and about 200,000 logical reads. Plan: Index Seek on
IX_Events_Customer, backward, then Top with an offset: every skipped row is read and discarded. The client already
holds the EventTime and EventID of the last row it showed. The API team will send them as @LastEventTime
datetime2(7) and @LastEventID bigint in place of @Skip from the next release; the first page is a separate call that
is already fast. Several events of one customer can share an EventTime.
data_notes: Azure SQL Database, General Purpose Gen5, 8 vCores, compatibility level 160. READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT ON. Query Store READ_WRITE. Collation SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS. All foreign keys are trusted. Statistics: auto create and auto update ON; a nightly job updates Orders, OrderLines and Payments with FULLSCAN.
Events: 900M rows, append-only, ~1.5M per day. Partner accounts have up to 40M events each.
baseline_sql: ORDER BY e.EventTime DESC, e.EventID DESC
OFFSET @Skip ROWS FETCH NEXT @Take ROWS ONLY;

correct_families.description: Seek straight to the row after the last one shown, using both sort columns, and read @Take rows.
reference_sql: ORDER BY e.EventTime DESC, e.EventID DESC;

traps.why: A predicate on EventTime alone skips the events that share the last timestamp shown.
traps.told_apart_by: Three events of the customer with one EventTime, with the page boundary after the first.
example_sql: ORDER BY e.EventTime DESC, e.EventID DESC;

traps.why: <= on the last key returns the last row of the previous page again.
traps.told_apart_by: Any page after the first: its first row repeats the previous page's last row.
example_sql: ORDER BY e.EventTime DESC, e.EventID DESC;

traps.why: Without EventID in ORDER BY, TOP can take any of the events that share a timestamp, so rows are skipped or repeated at the page boundary.
traps.told_apart_by: Three events of the customer with one EventTime at a page boundary.

traps.why: ROW_NUMBER with a range filter numbers every row up to the page, the same work as OFFSET.
example_sql: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY e.EventTime DESC, e.EventID DESC) AS rn

min_improvement.basis: A page at @Skip = 200,000 reads about 200,000 index rows. A keyset seek reads @Take rows.

key.reference_notes: The candidate takes @LastEventTime and @LastEventID where the baseline takes @Skip. To compare them, the live tier must set the two values to the EventTime and EventID of row number @Skip in the baseline order.
